intro: If you want a stay in central Tak that is comfortable to sleep in, clean, quiet and easy on the wallet, a name road-trippers passing through and people in town for work pick often is Silayok Grand Hotel. It's a 3-star midrange hotel on Mahatthai Bamrung Road in Rahaeng subdistrict, within walking distance of the Ping River, the evening market and city restaurants. body.html: Silayok Grand Hotel is a 3-star midrange hotel in central Mueang Tak, set on Mahatthai Bamrung Road in Rahaeng subdistrict. It's a simple, easy-to-use building rather than a luxury one, but what sets it apart from the usual budget stay is the comfortable beds, the clean, quiet rooms, and a carved-wood lobby that gives it real character. Road-trippers passing through Tak, people in town for work, or travelers stopping overnight before heading to Mae Sot, Umphang or Lampang often pick it because you sleep well here at a price that stays light.

Rooms range from Deluxe with twin beds to Deluxe with a queen bed. Inside you get air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, fridge, free bottled water, and an en suite bathroom with hot water. The most common praise is that the beds are soft, you sleep well, and the rooms are clean and quiet. The trade-off is that the bathrooms are plain and no-frills, the shower pressure in some rooms is weak, and the air-dried towels can be a little stiff. It's a good-value room to sleep in at a fair price, not a polished hotel that's flawless in every detail.

"Very soft bed, slept really well, and the room was clean and quiet. The lobby is lovely with its carved wood, the staff are friendly, and it's right in town — you can walk to the river and the evening market. Genuinely good value."

Service is another strong point. Staff get praised for being friendly and helpful, with some speaking English. There's an on-site restaurant, a massage room, a garden and terrace to relax in, roomy free parking and a 24-hour front desk. The limits reviews mention are that breakfast is very light — just toast and coffee — and the Wi-Fi password changes daily, so you have to ask for it again. The upside is the central location, with restaurants and food shops around to step out and find your own meals easily.

The central Tak location on Mahatthai Bamrung Road is a genuine plus. You can walk to the Ping River, the evening market and city restaurants, with convenience stores and food nearby. The trade-off is that the hotel is a little hard to find — several reviews suggest using GPS, since the signage isn't obvious and the entrance isn't clear. The overall score sits around 8.1 from real guest reviews, and TripAdvisor ranks it #2 of 9 hotels in Tak, with value, cleanliness and the beds standing out.

Honestly, Silayok Grand is not a boutique stay or a riverside resort, and there's no pool. Some reviews note the bathrooms are very plain, the water pressure is weak, breakfast is minimal, and the hotel is hard to locate. If you want a full Ping River resort feel, Viang Tak Riverside may suit better. But if you want a clean, quiet room with a comfortable bed, a central location and free parking at a light price — this place does the job well and is genuinely good value.

A tip from following the reviews here: set GPS to the hotel before you arrive, since the building is hard to find the first time. At check-in, test the shower pressure — if it's too weak, ask the front desk to change your room. Make the most of the free parking and central location: it's an easy walk out to the Ping River, the evening market and food. Compare direct rates against Agoda and Booking, since prices move by season. And because breakfast is very light, plan to head out for noodles or a local breakfast in town if you want something heartier.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Silayok Grand Hotel Tak

faq.q: Where is Silayok Grand Hotel and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 315/18 Mahatthai Bamrung Road, Rahaeng, Mueang Tak, right in central Tak — walkable to the Ping River, the evening market and city restaurants, with food shops nearby. Somdej Phra Chao Taksin Maharaj Hospital is about a 15-minute walk away. The hotel is a little hard to find, so it's best to navigate with GPS.

faq.q: How much does Silayok Grand Hotel cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at about ฿450/night for a Deluxe Twin. There's a budget Standard room around ฿400, plus a Deluxe Queen and a larger Deluxe room from roughly ฿550–690. Prices rise over holidays, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Silayok Grand Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for road-trippers passing through Tak, people in town for work, or anyone stopping overnight before Mae Sot, Umphang or Lampang who want a clean, quiet room, a comfortable bed and free parking at a light price, rather than a riverside resort vibe.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Silayok Grand Hotel clean and comfortable?
faq.a: The beds are soft, you sleep well, and the rooms are clean and quiet — the thing guests praise most. The trade-off is that the bathrooms are plain and no-frills, the shower pressure is weak in some rooms, and the air-dried towels can be a little stiff. It's worth testing the shower at check-in and telling the front desk if anything needs fixing.

faq.q: Does it have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: Yes — both breakfast and free, roomy parking, plus free Wi-Fi throughout, handy for self-drivers. One note is that breakfast is very light — just toast and coffee — so if you want something heartier, head out for a local breakfast in town. There's no pool here.

faq.q: What's Silayok Grand Hotel's review score — is it reliable?
faq.a: Silayok Grand Hotel has around 121 rooms and scores about 8.1 from real guest reviews, with TripAdvisor ranking it #2 of 9 hotels in Tak. Its strengths are value, cleanliness, the beds and the central location. It's a midrange hotel focused on value over luxury — a good fit if you want a clean, quiet room at a light price in central Tak.
